Morales+2025, with CARMENES+HARPS+HIRES+PFS and a baseline ~1900 d longer, fit b and c only; their residual periodogram shows power at 59.5 d (rotation) and ~20 d harmonics, and no ~400 d signal is mentioned. Recorded as unlikely. No TOI; no Gaia NSS. Mignon+2024 list 314.4 d and 236.5 d HARPS signals for GJ 317 in Table 5 but show in Sect. 6.2.2 they come from an erroneous offset correction; after fitting b and c the residual peaks at 50.9 and 59.4 d are rotation. Neither is a candidate, and neither matches Tuomi's 397.7 d.

incidental_finds_outside_my_scope.item: GJ 3929 c period on the confirmed tab may be the alias
incidental_finds_outside_my_scope.detail: planets_confirmed.csv gives GJ 3929 c P = 14.303 d (Kemmer+2022) with Msini 5.71 M_E. Beard+2022 (arXiv:2207.10672, abstract and Sect. 4.2) show 14.30 d and 15.04 d are aliases of one signal and adopt 15.04 +/- 0.03 d as the likely true period with Msini 5.71 +/- 0.92; NASA pscomppars uses 15.04 d. The row mixes the two solutions.

incidental_finds_outside_my_scope.item: GJ 682 b and c (on the confirmed tab) were disowned by their own discoverers
incidental_finds_outside_my_scope.detail: Tuomi et al. 2019 (arXiv:1906.04644, App. A.43), the same lead author as the 2014 discovery, could not recover the 17.48 d or 57.32 d signals once new HARPS data were added, and conclude that 'the interpretation of Tuomi et al. (2014) that there are two low-mass planets orbiting the star is invalid' and 'assume conservatively that these planets do not exist'. OEC lists both as Controversial; NASA and exoplanet.eu still list them as confirmed. Mignon+2024 (arXiv:2502.06513) did not recover them but blame too few HARPS nights. The writer may want to move them off the confirmed tab or flag them.
